description.description: The Atari 400 and 800 were the first home computers to use custom coprocessors and the first to use 'sprites' and special video interruptions like display lists, features that would be implemented many years later on the Amiga. It also offered high graphic resolution, color, and sound capabilities - more than what other machines could do at the time. The Atari 400 and 800 are internally identical - the 400 is the low-cost machine with 16K of RAM, vs the 800's 48KB of RAM. The 400 has one cartridge port (vs 2 for the 800) and has a membrane keyboard (800 has a typewriter-style keyboard).
